title: Why Do Dogs Love Racing Along The Fence Together?

script: Two dogs on either side of a fence, both sprinting at full speed in the same direction, and it looks intense, but it's almost always the opposite of a fight. This is a form of parallel play, and the fence itself is actually a big part of why it works so well. With a physical barrier between them, both dogs get all the thrill of a high-speed chase, full sprinting, matching pace, reacting to each other's movement, without any real risk of a collision or an actual confrontation. It lets two dogs who don't fully know each other yet, or who have very different play styles, safely enjoy that same explosive energy together. You'll usually see loose, bouncy bodies and relaxed faces the whole time, the real signs of play instead of aggression. So that fence-line sprint isn't a standoff, it's basically the safest, most satisfying version of tag two dogs can play. Want more real dog behavior insight? The link's below.
